guides.title: How to Set Multiple Timers on iPhone (iOS 17+)
guides.excerpt: Run multiple concurrent timers on iPhone — Clock app, Siri voice commands, named timers, Live Activities.
guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

iOS 17 and later supports multiple concurrent timers on iPhone. Open Clock > Timers, tap the plus icon in the top-right corner, and add a new named timer alongside your running one. Each timer can have its own label, duration, and alert sound. The Live Activity on the lock screen shows up to four timers at once.

When Did Multiple Timers Come to iPhone?

For more than a decade, the iOS Clock app supported only a single timer — a long-standing frustration for cooks who wanted to track pasta and bread simultaneously, or for fitness users running interval workouts. iOS 17, released in September 2023, finally added multi-timer support. Every iPhone capable of running iOS 17 (iPhone XS and later) has the feature.

How Do You Add a Second Timer in the Clock App?

  1. Open the Clock app and tap the Timers tab.
  2. If a timer is already running, you will see it at the top of the screen.
  3. Tap the plus icon in the top-right corner.
  4. Scroll the wheels to set duration, tap Label to name the timer (e.g., "Pasta"), and choose an alert sound.
  5. Tap Start. Both timers now run side by side.

You can repeat this to add a third, fourth, or more timers. There is no practical upper limit — the Clock app handles many simultaneous timers gracefully.

How Do You Name a Timer on iPhone?

When creating a new timer, tap the Label field above the duration wheel. Type a short name — "Pasta," "Tea," "Bread," "Workout Round 1." The label appears in the timer list and in the lock screen Live Activity, making it easy to identify which timer just ended when multiple are running.

How Do You Use Siri to Set Multiple Named Timers?

Siri understands named timers in iOS 17+. Useful phrasings:

  • "Hey Siri, set a pasta timer for 9 minutes."
  • "Hey Siri, set a bread timer for 25 minutes."
  • "Hey Siri, how much time is left on my pasta timer?"
  • "Hey Siri, cancel the bread timer."
  • "Hey Siri, add 2 minutes to the pasta timer."

Siri identifies each timer by its name when answering, so you do not need to look at the screen.

What Does the Lock Screen Live Activity Show?

The iOS Live Activity on the lock screen shows the timer label, remaining duration, and a circular progress arc. With multiple timers running, up to four are visible at once as stacked pills. Tap any one to expand or dismiss. The Dynamic Island on iPhone 14 Pro and later models also shows the closest-to-finish timer as a live count in the pill.

What Are Practical Uses for Multiple iPhone Timers?

Use CaseTimer 1Timer 2Timer 3
Pasta dinnerPasta (9 min)Sauce (15 min)Garlic bread (8 min)
Bread bakingFirst proof (60 min)Second proof (30 min)Bake (45 min)
Tabata workoutWork (20 sec)Rest (10 sec)Round complete
Pomodoro workFocus (25 min)Short break (5 min)Long break (15 min)
Tea serviceGreen (2 min)Black (4 min)Herbal (6 min)
ChildcareBedtime (15 min)Story (10 min)Lights out (5 min)

What About iOS 16 and Earlier?

iOS 16 and earlier officially support only one Clock-app timer. The historical workaround was to set additional alarms with custom labels in the Alarm tab of the Clock app, or use a third-party app like Multi Timer. On iOS 17, the native solution makes those workarounds unnecessary.

Can the Apple Watch Show iPhone's Multiple Timers?

Yes. Open the Timers app on Apple Watch (watchOS 10+); all timers from the paired iPhone appear in the list. The Watch can pause, cancel, or add minutes to any of them. The haptic tap on the wrist fires when each timer ends, with a unique haptic per timer if labeled distinctly.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many timers can iPhone run at once?

There is no documented hard limit. We tested 20 simultaneous timers and all fired on schedule.

Can each iPhone timer have a different sound?

Yes. Tap When Timer Ends inside each timer's settings to pick a unique alert sound.

Do multiple iPhone timers work on iPad?

Yes. iPadOS 17 added the same Clock app multi-timer feature.

Can I rearrange my iPhone timers?

Timers display in start order. To rearrange, cancel and re-create in the order you want.

What if two timers end at the same moment?

Both alerts play sequentially with a slight stagger, each labeled by its name in the notification.

Why don't I see the plus icon?

You are running iOS 16 or earlier. Update to iOS 17 (Settings > General > Software Update) on any iPhone XS or newer.

For full citations and methodology, see our sources page.

guides.title: How to Set a Timer on Apple Watch (Digital Crown, Siri, Complications)
guides.excerpt: How to set a timer on Apple Watch — Digital Crown, Siri voice, complications, multi-timer in watchOS 10.
guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

To set a timer on Apple Watch: open the Timer app, scroll the Digital Crown to choose a duration, and tap Start — or raise your wrist and say "Hey Siri, set a 5 minute timer." The Timer complication on most watch faces gives one-tap access. Apple Watch syncs running timers with the paired iPhone, so a timer started on either device runs on both.

How Do You Open the Apple Watch Timer App?

The Timer app ships preinstalled on every Apple Watch. From any watch face, press the Digital Crown to open the app grid (or list view), scroll to the orange Timer icon, and tap. Alternatively, hold the Digital Crown briefly, say "Hey Siri, open Timer," and the app launches.

How Do You Set a Timer With the Digital Crown?

  1. Open the Timer app on the watch.
  2. Tap a preset (1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 30 minutes, 1 hour) for one-tap start.
  3. Or tap Custom, then rotate the Digital Crown to set hours, minutes, and seconds individually.
  4. Tap the green Start button.

The Digital Crown's haptic feedback makes setting a duration on the small screen feel deliberate — each minute increment produces a tiny tactile click.

How Do You Use Siri to Set a Timer on Apple Watch?

The wrist-raise-and-talk pattern is the fastest way to start a timer on Apple Watch. Raise your wrist (or press and hold the Digital Crown) and say:

  • "Hey Siri, set a 5 minute timer."
  • "Hey Siri, set a pasta timer for 9 minutes." (named timer, watchOS 10+)
  • "Hey Siri, stop the timer."
  • "Hey Siri, how much time is left?"

On Apple Watch Series 7 and later, "Hey Siri" detection is on-device and works without an internet connection for timer commands. The processing happens locally, which makes voice timers faster and more reliable than they were on earlier models.

How Do You Add a Timer Complication to the Watch Face?

A Timer complication on your watch face means setting a timer takes one tap from any screen.

  1. Long-press the watch face on the watch (or open the Watch app on iPhone > Faces).
  2. Tap Edit.
  3. Swipe to the Complications screen.
  4. Tap a complication slot and choose Timer.
  5. Save the face.

The Modular, Infograph, and Wayfinder faces all support a Timer complication.

What Happens When the Timer Ends?

Apple Watch fires a strong haptic tap on the wrist accompanied by a chime. If you do not respond within a few seconds, the haptic repeats with increasing intensity. Tap the dismiss button or cover the watch face with your other hand to silence it. The "Cover to Mute" gesture must be enabled in Settings > Sounds & Haptics.

watchOS Version Differences

watchOSReleasedMulti-timerNamed timersOn-device Siri
watchOS 102023YesYesYes
watchOS 92022NoPartialYes (Series 7+)
watchOS 82021NoNoSeries 7+ only
watchOS 72020NoNoNo

Can Apple Watch Run a Timer Independently of iPhone?

Yes. Once a timer is set, it runs on the Watch's own processor and will fire even if the paired iPhone is dead, off, or far out of range. This is one of the advantages of the Watch as a kitchen timer — the iPhone can be charging in another room while the Watch ticks down on your wrist.

Does the Apple Watch Have a Pomodoro Timer?

Not natively, but the multi-timer feature in watchOS 10 makes Pomodoro straightforward — set a 25 minute focus timer and a 5 minute break timer side by side. Several third-party Pomodoro apps (Be Focused, Focus To-Do) include Watch apps for richer Pomodoro workflows. For browser users, see our Pomodoro timer.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Apple Watch timer work when the watch is on the charger?

Yes. The timer continues counting while charging; if it ends, the chime and haptic still fire.

Can I set a timer longer than 24 hours on Apple Watch?

The custom timer goes up to 99 hours 59 minutes 59 seconds. For longer durations, use an alarm instead.

How do I stop the Apple Watch timer haptic?

Tap the timer notification, or use the Cover to Mute gesture (palm over the watch face for three seconds).

Why doesn't my Watch timer sync with iPhone?

Check that Bluetooth is on and the watch is paired. The sync uses iCloud and Continuity, so signing out and back in to iCloud usually resolves stuck states.

Can I set a timer from the Apple Watch keypad?

The Timer app uses the Digital Crown rather than a numeric keypad, but you can also dictate the duration using Scribble or voice.

Does Apple Watch have a stopwatch?

Yes. The Stopwatch app is separate from Timer and supports lap timing.

For full citations and methodology, see our sources page.

guides.title: How to Set a Timer on Mac (Spotlight, Clock App, Siri)
guides.excerpt: Every way to set a timer on Mac: Clock app, Siri, Spotlight, Terminal, Reminders. Verified against Apple's current macOS documentation.
guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, productivity researcher at The Blog Timer. Updated 2026-07-31.

The fastest way to set a timer on a Mac: press Command-Space, type "set a timer for 10 minutes," and press Return. Since macOS Ventura the Mac also has a proper Clock app with a Timers tab, Siri takes timer requests by voice, and Terminal can rig a countdown in one line. This guide covers each method, checked against Apple's current Clock documentation, including the details most articles get wrong, like what happens when the lid closes.

The Clock app (macOS Ventura and later)

macOS Ventura brought the iPhone's Clock app to the Mac, with world clocks, alarms, a stopwatch, and timers. Apple's steps for setting a timer in Clock are short: open Clock, click Timers at the top of the window (or choose View > Timers), set the duration, and click Start. You can pause and resume mid-count, and each timer takes a label and its own alert sound.

Two facts from Apple's documentation are worth calling out because guides routinely get them backwards. First, running multiple timers at once requires macOS 14.2 or later; on Ventura you get one at a time. Second, in Apple's own words, a timer "continues even if you open another app or if your Mac goes to sleep." Closing the lid does not kill your countdown. The alert fires when the timer ends.

Siri: the hands-free method

With Siri enabled (System Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri, or Siri & Spotlight on older versions), a spoken "set a timer for 25 minutes" starts a countdown without touching the keyboard. Apple's Clock guide uses the example "set a pizza timer for 12 minutes," and the label sticks, so several named timers can run side by side on macOS 14.2+. The full activation options, menu bar icon, keyboard shortcut, or voice trigger, are in Apple's Siri on Mac guide. Kitchen scenario, flour on both hands: this is the method.

Spotlight: the keyboard method

Apple's Spotlight guide lists Command-Space as the shortcut, and Spotlight now handles actions, not just search. Press Command-Space, type a timer phrase like "timer 25 minutes," and press Return; the request is handed to the timer system and a countdown starts without opening any app window. For people who live on the keyboard this is the quickest route by a wide margin, and it works from inside any full-screen app.

Terminal: the tinkerer's method

No Clock app needed. This one-liner waits five minutes, then plays a system sound:

sleep 300 && afplay /System/Library/Sounds/Glass.aiff

The sounds folder on every Mac ships fourteen options; I checked mine while writing this: Basso, Blow, Bottle, Frog, Funk, Glass, Hero, Morse, Ping, Pop, Purr, Sosumi, Submarine, and Tink. Swap the filename to taste, or use say "time is up" for a spoken alert. One caveat: a sleeping Mac pauses a shell script, unlike a Clock timer. If the countdown must survive with the lid open but idle, chain in caffeinate, which keeps the system awake for a set period: caffeinate -t 300 && afplay /System/Library/Sounds/Glass.aiff. That trick doubles as a way to keep the Mac from dozing off during a Pomodoro session.

Reminders: the labeled-notification method

For countdowns where the message matters more than the ring ("take the cake out," "join the standup"), create a reminder with a time instead. Reminders notifications carry text, survive restarts, and sync to your iPhone and Watch through iCloud, which no local timer does. It is less a timer than a scheduled nudge, and for anything over an hour that distinction favors Reminders.

Browser: the no-version-requirement method

On a Mac too old for the Clock app, or a locked-down work machine, a browser timer needs nothing installed: open our 25-minute timer or any other duration and the countdown starts in the tab. Keep the tab visible or audible; the reasons background tabs throttle timers are covered in our timer accuracy guide. Windows users can find the equivalent native methods in how to set a timer on Windows.

Method comparison

MethodRequiresMultiple timersSurvives sleepBest for
Clock appmacOS Ventura+Yes (macOS 14.2+)YesLabeled, reliable countdowns
Siri voiceSiri enabledYes (macOS 14.2+)YesHands busy, kitchen
SpotlightmacOS Ventura+Yes (macOS 14.2+)YesKeyboard-first speed
TerminalAny macOSOne per windowNo (use caffeinate)Scripts and tinkering
RemindersAny macOSYesYes, plus restartsLong, labeled countdowns
Browser timerAny browserMulti-tabWhile awakeNo install, any Mac

If the timer never rings

The usual suspects, in the order worth checking: system volume muted or near zero; notifications for the Clock app switched off under System Settings > Notifications; or a Focus mode quietly swallowing alerts, which is easy to trigger by accident when Focus syncs across your Apple devices. If a scheduled Focus turns on from your iPhone, your Mac timer goes silent with it. Thirty seconds with a test timer after changing any of these settings saves a burnt dinner later.

Older Macs, before Ventura

On Monterey and earlier there is no Clock app. Siri still takes timer requests on those systems, third-party menu bar timer utilities fill the gap for a glanceable countdown, and the Terminal and browser methods above work on any vintage. If you are choosing between upgrade paths purely for timer quality, the Clock app plus the 14.2 multiple-timers feature is a real, if small, quality-of-life gain.

For full citations and methodology, see our sources page.

guides.title: How to Set a Timer on Windows 11 (Clock App, Cortana, Focus Sessions)
guides.excerpt: How to set a timer on Windows — Clock app, Focus Sessions, Cortana, Copilot, PowerShell, browser.
guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

To set a timer on Windows 11: open the Clock app from the Start menu, click the Timer tab, set a duration, and press Start. For voice control, say "Hey Cortana, set a timer for 10 minutes" if Cortana is enabled, or use any browser-based timer in Edge or Chrome. Windows 11 simplified the Clock app significantly compared to Windows 10.

How Do You Open the Windows Clock App?

The Windows Clock app is preinstalled on Windows 10 and Windows 11. Press the Start button, type "clock," and click the Clock app result. The app has four tabs: Focus Sessions, Timer, Alarm, World Clock, and Stopwatch.

How Do You Set a Timer in Windows Clock?

  1. Open the Clock app.
  2. Click the Timer tab in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the plus icon in the bottom-right to add a new timer (or click the edit pencil on an existing tile).
  4. Enter hours, minutes, and seconds, plus an optional name.
  5. Click Save, then click the play arrow on the timer tile.

Saved timers persist between sessions — useful if you reuse the same durations daily.

How Do You Use Focus Sessions in Windows 11 Clock?

Windows 11 added a Focus Sessions feature to the Clock app — effectively a built-in Pomodoro. Open Clock > Focus Sessions, choose a session length (15-240 minutes), and the app guides you through a focused work block with optional 5-minute breaks every 30 minutes. It integrates with Spotify (background music) and Microsoft To Do (link tasks to focus sessions).

This is the closest thing to a native Pomodoro timer on Windows. For more comprehensive Pomodoro options, see our best Pomodoro apps roundup.

How Do You Set a Timer With Cortana?

If Cortana is enabled — note that Microsoft is deprecating Cortana as a standalone assistant in favor of Copilot — say "Hey Cortana, set a timer for 10 minutes." Cortana replies and the timer fires a notification when complete.

On newer Windows 11 builds (2024+), Microsoft is integrating timer commands into Copilot. The exact phrasing varies, but "set a timer" works in both.

How Do You Set a Timer From PowerShell?

For scripting and developer workflows:

Start-Sleep -Seconds 300; [console]::beep(1000,500)

This pauses for 5 minutes (300 seconds) and then beeps. You can chain commands to run a notification or play a sound file. PowerShell timers are command-line only — there is no visual countdown by default, though you can add one with a progress bar.

What Changed in Windows 11 Clock vs Windows 10?

FeatureWindows 10Windows 11
App nameAlarms & ClockClock
Multiple timersYesYes
Focus SessionsNoYes (Pomodoro)
Spotify integrationNoYes
Microsoft To Do integrationNoYes
UI designFluentMica + WinUI 3

How Do You Set a Timer From the Browser on Windows?

The fastest no-install timer on Windows is a browser tab. Type "5 minute timer" into Google Search or open our 5-minute timer. The browser tab handles countdown and sound; pinning the tab in Microsoft Edge or Chrome keeps it always accessible.

Does Windows Have a Pomodoro Timer Built In?

Yes, via Focus Sessions in the Clock app (Windows 11 only). For Windows 10 users or those who want more control over interval lengths, third-party apps like Pomodoro Timer or our browser-based Pomodoro timer work well.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does my Windows timer not make a sound?

Check Settings > System > Notifications and confirm Clock is allowed to play sounds. Also check that the system volume mixer has the Clock app unmuted.

Can I set multiple timers in Windows Clock?

Yes. Each saved timer tile can be started and run concurrently with others.

Does the Windows timer work when the PC sleeps?

No — system sleep suspends the timer. Use the Wake Timer feature in Power Options to schedule a wake event for important alerts.

How do I delete a timer in Windows Clock?

Right-click a timer tile and choose Delete, or click the edit pencil and then the trash icon.

Is there a keyboard shortcut to start a Windows timer?

Not natively. Some third-party tools like AutoHotkey can bind a hotkey to launch a timer.

Can I use Copilot to set a timer?

Yes, on Windows 11 with Copilot enabled. Say "set a timer for 10 minutes" through Copilot voice or the chat input.

For full citations and methodology, see our sources page.

guides.title: How Long to Bake a Potato (Russet, Sweet, Foil, by Size)
guides.excerpt: Bake times for russet and sweet potatoes by size, oven temperature, foil vs naked, microwave and air fryer.
guides.author: Suraj Giri

sources.author: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperatures

guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

Bake a russet potato at 425°F (218°C) for 45-60 minutes for the classic crispy-skin, fluffy-interior result. Sweet potatoes need 45-50 minutes at the same temperature. Smaller potatoes finish faster (35-40 min); large bakers may need 75 minutes. The potato is done when a fork or paring knife slides through with zero resistance — internal temperature 205-210°F (96-99°C). Use our 45-minute timer or 60-minute timer.

How Long to Bake a Russet Potato?

The russet potato is the gold standard for baking — its high starch content and low moisture produce the fluffy, dry interior most cooks want. At 425°F (218°C), a medium russet (8-10 oz) bakes in 45-55 minutes; a large baker (12-16 oz) takes 60-75 minutes. The USDA notes that potatoes must reach an internal temperature of at least 205°F (96°C) for the starch granules to fully gelatinize and the interior to achieve the desired flaky texture.

A faster method: 450°F (232°C) for 40-50 minutes — slightly crisper skin, marginally less even interior. A slower method: 350°F (177°C) for 75-90 minutes — gentler, particularly good when baking multiple potatoes alongside a roast.

How Long to Bake a Sweet Potato?

A sweet potato at 425°F (218°C) takes 45-50 minutes for a medium tuber, 55-70 minutes for a large one. The sugars caramelize when the sweet potato is fully cooked — a good visual cue is seeing dark, sticky syrup oozing from any cracks in the skin. Internal temperature 205-210°F (96-99°C), same as russet.

Foil-Wrapped vs Naked Baking: Which Is Better?

The Idaho Potato Commission and most professional cooks recommend baking potatoes unwrapped, rubbed with oil and salt, directly on the oven rack. Foil traps steam, which steams the potato rather than baking it — the result is a soft, gummy skin and a denser interior. Foil is acceptable if you plan to hold the potato hot for serving (it keeps temperature longer in foil) or if you genuinely prefer soft skin.

Baking Times by Size and Temperature

Potato SizeWeight425°F400°F350°F
Small5-7 oz35-40 min45-50 min55-65 min
Medium8-10 oz45-55 min55-65 min70-80 min
Large baker12-16 oz60-75 min70-85 min90-100 min
Extra large16-20 oz75-90 min85-100 min105-120 min
Sweet potato (med)8-10 oz45-55 min55-65 min70-80 min

How Long in the Microwave?

For a fast result, microwave the potato for 5-8 minutes on high (a 1000W microwave; adjust proportionally for other wattages), pierce the skin first, and rest 2 minutes before opening. The skin will be soft, not crisp — for crisp skin, finish in a 450°F oven for 10 minutes after microwaving. This hybrid method delivers a baked potato in 20 minutes total.

How Long in the Air Fryer?

Air-fryer baked potatoes at 400°F (204°C) take 35-40 minutes for a medium russet — faster than the oven and with crispier skin thanks to the high air velocity. Rub with oil and salt, place directly on the basket. See our broader air fryer cooking guide for technique parallels.

What Internal Temperature Means Done?

A baked potato is done when the internal temperature reaches 205-210°F (96-99°C), measured with an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the potato. Lower temperatures leave starch granules incompletely gelatinized, producing a denser, less fluffy interior. The fork-resistance test correlates well with this temperature in practice.

Why Do You Pierce a Baked Potato?

Piercing the skin with a fork in 4-6 places lets steam escape during baking. An unpierced potato can — rarely but dramatically — explode in the oven as superheated steam builds inside the skin. Even when explosion doesn't happen, piercing reduces the risk of a soggy interior caused by trapped moisture.

How to Tell When a Baked Potato Is Done

  1. Fork test. A fork or paring knife slides into the thickest part with no resistance.
  2. Squeeze test. The potato gives slightly to gentle pressure (use a kitchen towel — the potato is hot).
  3. Thermometer. Internal temperature 205-210°F (96-99°C).
  4. Skin appearance. Skin is crisped, slightly papery, and the salt rub has darkened.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long to bake potatoes at 400 degrees?

About 55-65 minutes for a medium russet at 400°F (204°C). Slightly slower than 425°F but more forgiving when timing other dishes.

Can I bake potatoes in foil?

Yes, but the skin will be soft rather than crisp. Foil is best when holding potatoes hot for later service.

How long to bake small potatoes?

Small potatoes (5-7 oz) bake in 35-40 minutes at 425°F.

Should I bake potatoes covered or uncovered?

Uncovered, rubbed with oil and salt, directly on the oven rack — this produces the classic baked-potato texture.

How long to bake multiple potatoes?

Time stays roughly the same as baking one — about 45-55 minutes for medium russets at 425°F — provided the oven is preheated and the potatoes are spaced for airflow.

Why is my baked potato hard inside?

Underbaked. Internal temperature didn't reach 205°F. Return to the oven for another 10-15 minutes and re-test with a fork.

Can I bake potatoes ahead?

Yes. Bake fully, then hold wrapped in foil in a warm oven (170-200°F) for up to an hour without significant texture loss.

How long do leftover baked potatoes keep?

Per USDA food safety guidelines, refrigerate within 2 hours and consume within 3-4 days.

For full citations and methodology, see our sources page.

guides.title: How Long to Grill Steak (by Cut, Thickness, Doneness)
guides.excerpt: Steak grilling times by cut, thickness, and target doneness — including two-zone method and USDA temps.
guides.author: Suraj Giri

sources.author: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperatures

sources.author: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
sources.title: Food Code, 2022

guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

For a 1-inch thick steak on a hot grill (450-500°F): 3-4 minutes per side for rare, 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, 5-6 minutes for medium, 7+ minutes for medium-well. Use the two-zone grilling method for thicker cuts. The USDA recommended internal temperature for steak is 145°F (63°C) with a 3-minute rest. A meat thermometer is the only reliable way to hit doneness consistently.

How Long to Grill Steak by Thickness?

Steak grilling time depends on three variables: thickness, target doneness, and grill temperature. The chart below assumes a hot grill (450-500°F / 232-260°C) and a steak brought to room temperature for 30 minutes before grilling.

ThicknessRare (125°F)Medium-Rare (135°F)Medium (145°F)Medium-Well (150°F)
1/2 inch1-2 min/side2 min/side2-3 min/side3 min/side
3/4 inch2-3 min/side3-4 min/side4 min/side4-5 min/side
1 inch3-4 min/side4-5 min/side5-6 min/side6-7 min/side
1.5 inch5-6 min/side6-7 min/side7-8 min/side9-10 min/side
2 inchTwo-zone methodTwo-zone methodTwo-zone methodTwo-zone method

What Are the USDA Internal Temperatures?

The USDA publishes minimum safe internal temperatures, but most home cooks aim for chef-recommended temperatures that prioritize texture and flavor over the minimum safety floor.

DonenessPull TempFinal Temp (after rest)Color
Rare120°F (49°C)125°F (52°C)Cool red center
Medium-rare130°F (54°C)135°F (57°C)Warm red center
Medium140°F (60°C)145°F (63°C)Warm pink center
Medium-well145°F (63°C)150°F (66°C)Slight pink
Well-done155°F (68°C)160°F (71°C)Brown throughout

Always pull the steak about 5°F below your target — carryover cooking continues during the rest. The USDA minimum for ground beef is 160°F, but for whole-muscle steak the minimum is 145°F with a 3-minute rest.

What Is Two-Zone Grilling?

For thick steaks (1.5 inches or more) or for tender cuts like filet mignon, build a two-zone fire. Pile charcoal or set burners to high on one side and leave the other side cool. Sear the steak over high heat for 1-2 minutes per side until a dark crust forms, then move it to the cool side, close the lid, and finish to target internal temperature using indirect heat.

This method, sometimes called the reverse sear when done in opposite order (low heat first, then high sear), produces a thick, edge-to-edge pink interior without overcooking the outer band. Meathead Goldwyn and other grilling experts consider it the gold standard for thick cuts.

Grilling Times by Cut

CutTypical ThicknessMedium-Rare TimeNotes
Ribeye1-1.5 in8-10 min totalHigh fat, forgives variation
NY Strip1-1.25 in8-10 min totalTighter grain, watch closely
Filet Mignon1.5-2 in10-14 min, two-zoneLean, easy to overcook
T-Bone / Porterhouse1.25-2 in10-14 min, two-zoneStrip side cooks faster than filet
Flank Steak3/4 in4-6 min/sideSlice thin against grain
Skirt Steak1/2 in2-3 min/sideHot and fast
Hanger3/4-1 in4-5 min/sideReverse sear works well

Why Does Resting Matter?

When meat cooks, juices migrate toward the cooler center. Resting the steak for 3-5 minutes after grilling allows those juices to redistribute throughout the muscle. A steak cut immediately after grilling loses 30-40% more juice on the cutting board than one rested for 5 minutes. The Maillard reaction that produces the crust also continues briefly during rest, deepening flavor.

How Do You Check Doneness Without a Thermometer?

The palm test is a workable shortcut. Press the fleshy part of your palm below the thumb with your other index finger. Relaxed hand = rare. Touch thumb to index finger = medium-rare. Thumb to middle = medium. Thumb to ring = medium-well. Thumb to pinky = well-done. The corresponding firmness in the steak indicates doneness. The palm test is approximate — a $15 instant-read thermometer is dramatically more reliable.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long to grill a 1-inch steak medium-rare?

About 4-5 minutes per side on a 450-500°F grill, pulled at 130°F internal, rested 5 minutes.

Should I close the grill lid?

For thicker steaks (1 inch+), close the lid to encourage even heat. For thinner cuts, open lid for higher direct heat.

How long to grill steak well-done?

7-9 minutes per side for a 1-inch steak; pull at 155°F. Carryover brings it to 160°F.

What temperature should my grill be?

450-500°F (232-260°C) for direct grilling. Hotter chars the exterior before the interior cooks; cooler leaves a pale crust.

How long should steak rest after grilling?

3-5 minutes for steaks up to 1.5 inches; 5-10 minutes for thicker cuts.

Can I grill steak from frozen?

Yes — Cook's Illustrated has shown that frozen steak grills well, taking about 50% longer per side, with a deeper crust and less gray band. Salt heavily and grill at lower-than-usual temperature.

How do I get grill marks on a steak?

Place the steak on a clean, oiled, very hot grate. Don't move it for the first half of the cook time per side, then rotate 90 degrees for cross-hatching.

How long to grill a tomahawk steak?

Tomahawks (typically 2-2.5 inches thick) require reverse-sear: 30-45 minutes indirect at 250°F until 110°F internal, then 1-2 minutes per side over high heat.

For full citations and methodology, see our sources page.

guides.title: How Long to Roast a Turkey (by Weight, Stuffed, Spatchcock)
guides.excerpt: Turkey roasting times by weight, with brining, spatchcock, deep-fry, and convection alternatives.
guides.author: Suraj Giri

sources.author: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperatures

sources.author: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
sources.title: Food Code, 2022

guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

Roast an unstuffed turkey at 325°F (163°C) for approximately 13 minutes per pound — so an 8-pound bird takes about 2 hours, a 14-pound bird about 3 hours, and a 20-pound bird about 4.5 hours. The USDA requires an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) measured in the thickest part of the thigh and breast.

How Long to Roast a Turkey by Weight?

At 325°F (163°C), the standard USDA-recommended roasting temperature for turkey, expect approximately:

Turkey WeightUnstuffedStuffed
8-12 lb2.75 - 3 hr3 - 3.5 hr
12-14 lb3 - 3.75 hr3.5 - 4 hr
14-18 lb3.75 - 4.25 hr4 - 4.25 hr
18-20 lb4.25 - 4.5 hr4.25 - 4.75 hr
20-24 lb4.5 - 5 hr4.75 - 5.25 hr

These are USDA estimates for a fully thawed turkey starting at refrigerator temperature in a preheated oven. Convection ovens cook roughly 25% faster — use the same internal-temperature target.

What Is the Safe Internal Temperature for Turkey?

Per the USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service, turkey must reach 165°F (74°C) measured in three places:

  1. The thickest part of the breast, away from bone.
  2. The innermost part of the thigh, not touching bone.
  3. The innermost part of the wing.

If the turkey is stuffed, the stuffing itself must also reach 165°F — this is why stuffed birds take longer. Many chefs pull the breast at 155°F and rely on the 10°F of carryover during a 30-minute rest, producing juicier meat. The USDA does not endorse this practice but it is standard in restaurant kitchens.

How Does Brining Affect Cook Time?

A wet-brined turkey cooks roughly 10-15% faster than an unbrined bird because the salt solution conducts heat more effectively than dry meat. A 14-pound brined turkey may finish in 2.5-2.75 hours instead of 3-3.75. Start checking internal temperature 30 minutes earlier than the chart suggests.

Dry brining (salt rubbed on the skin 24-72 hours ahead, no liquid) does not significantly change cook time but produces crispier skin.

Spatchcock vs Whole Turkey: Cook Time Difference?

A spatchcocked turkey — backbone removed, bird flattened — cooks dramatically faster than a whole turkey because the meat lies in a single plane and heat penetrates evenly. A 14-pound spatchcocked turkey roasts in 75-90 minutes at 425°F, compared to 3+ hours whole. The breast and thigh also finish closer to simultaneously, eliminating the chronic problem of dry breast meat alongside underdone thighs.

How Long to Deep-Fry a Turkey?

A deep-fried turkey cooks at 3-4 minutes per pound at 350°F (177°C) peanut oil. A 12-pound turkey finishes in 36-48 minutes. Critical safety note: the National Fire Protection Association reports that deep-fryer fires cause more than 1,000 home fires annually in the United States. The turkey must be fully thawed and dried; partial ice causes oil to violently boil over.

Cooking Method Comparison

MethodTemperature14-lb Turkey TimeResult
Roast (oven)325°F3 - 3.75 hrTraditional, even browning
High-heat roast425°F initial, then 325°F2.5 - 3 hrCrispier skin
Spatchcock425°F1.5 hrEven, fast, modern favorite
Deep-fry350°F oil42-56 minCrispy skin, juicy meat
Smoked225-275°F5-7 hrDeep smoke flavor
Convection oven300°F (-25 from std)2.25 - 3 hr25% faster, even crisping

How Long to Thaw a Frozen Turkey?

Per USDA: in the refrigerator, allow 24 hours per 4-5 pounds of turkey. A 16-pound turkey needs about 4 days. In cold water (change every 30 minutes), allow 30 minutes per pound — a 16-pound turkey thaws in 8 hours. Never thaw at room temperature.

Why Does Resting Matter for Turkey?

A roasted turkey must rest at least 30 minutes, ideally 45, before carving. The 10-pound-plus mass continues to cook 5-10°F during rest, and the rest period lets juices redistribute throughout the meat. Carving immediately produces dry meat and a flooded cutting board.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long to roast a 15 pound turkey?

About 3.25-3.75 hours unstuffed at 325°F, or 1.5-1.75 hours spatchcocked at 425°F.

What temperature should I roast a turkey at?

325°F (163°C) is the USDA-recommended standard. 425°F works for spatchcocked or high-heat methods.

How long does a 20 pound turkey take?

About 4.25-4.5 hours unstuffed at 325°F. Plan for 5 hours with rest time included.

Should I cover the turkey with foil?

Optional. Tenting with foil for the first hour and removing for the final hour produces crispier skin without overbrowning.

Should I stuff the turkey?

Food safety experts recommend baking stuffing separately. If stuffing inside the bird, ensure stuffing center reaches 165°F.

How do I keep turkey breast from drying out?

Brine, dry-brine, or butter-baste. Pull the breast at 155°F and let carryover finish the cook.

Can I roast turkey from frozen?

The USDA permits roasting from frozen — it takes about 50% longer than a thawed bird and you cannot stuff a frozen turkey.

How long does cooked turkey keep?

Per USDA, refrigerated cooked turkey keeps 3-4 days; frozen, 2-6 months.

For full citations and methodology, see our sources page.

guides.title: How Long to Cook Rice (White, Brown, Basmati & Jasmine Times)
guides.excerpt: Stovetop times for every common rice: white long-grain, basmati and jasmine cook 15 minutes; brown rice 45-50 minutes. Includes water ratios, method, food safety (USDA FSIS) and troubleshooting.
guides.author: Suraj Giri

sources.author: Food
sources.title: All About Cooking Rice — UNL Food (University of Nebraska–Lincoln Extension)

sources.author: Fsis
sources.title: Leftovers and Food Safety — USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

sources.author: Foodsmartcolorado
sources.title: Brown Rice — Food Smart Colorado (Colorado State University)

guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, researcher at The Blog Timer. Updated 2026-08-09.

The short answer: 15 minutes for white, 45 for brown

Cook long-grain white rice, basmati, and jasmine for 15 minutes in a covered pot (up to about 18 minutes on a low-output burner). Brown rice takes 45-50 minutes because the bran layer resists water. The real variable is the water ratio: white long-grain needs 1¾-2 cups of liquid per cup of dry rice, while brown needs 2-2½ cups. Set a 15-minute timer for white, a 45-minute timer for brown, keep the lid on the whole time, then rest off the heat.

The stovetop method, step by step

This is the absorption method, which is what the standard cooking times below assume. It works for white, brown, basmati, and jasmine.

  1. Measure and rinse. Combine 1 cup dry rice with the liquid listed in the table. Rinse white rice in a fine mesh strainer until the water runs nearly clear to remove surface starch.
  2. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
  3. Cover and drop to a bare simmer. The moment it boils, put on a tight lid and turn the heat to low. Do not lift the lid again while it cooks — escaping steam is the most common cause of crunchy rice.
  4. Cook for the listed time. 15 minutes for white long-grain, basmati, and jasmine; 45-50 minutes for brown.
  5. Rest 5-10 minutes off the heat, still covered, then fluff with a fork. If the rice is not quite tender or liquid remains, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln Extension advises replacing the lid and cooking 2 to 4 minutes longer (UNL Food, "All About Cooking Rice").

Cooking time and water ratio by variety

The times in this table come from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln Extension's published rice cooking chart (UNL Food). Basmati and jasmine are long-grain white rices and follow the long-grain row. Quantities are per 1 cup of uncooked rice on a stovetop.

Rice varietyLiquid (per 1 cup dry rice)Cooking timeNotes
Long-grain white (incl. basmati, jasmine)1¾ to 2 cups15 minutesRinse first; rest 5-10 min off heat
Medium- or short-grain white1½ cups15 minutesStickier texture (sushi, risotto styles)
Brown rice (long or short grain)2 to 2½ cups45 to 50 minutesBran layer slows absorption
Converted / parboiled rice2 to 2½ cups20 to 25 minutesPartially precooked at the mill
Instant / precooked riceFollow package~5 minutesFully cooked; just rehydrate

Brown rice's longer time is structural, not optional: the intact bran and germ are waxy and slow water penetration, which is why even fully cooked brown rice holds a chewier bite (Food Smart Colorado, Colorado State University). The same site notes parboiled brown rice cuts the cook time to roughly 10 minutes.

What actually changes the cooking time

Burner output. "Low" on a weak stove barely simmers, which is why the same white rice can take 15 minutes on one range and 18 on another. If yours runs cool, use the 18-minute timer as the floor and check at 15.

Water ratio. Too much water and the 15-minute cook finishes into mush; too little and the bottom scorches before the grain softens. Stay inside the UNL ranges (1¾-2 cups for long-grain white; 2-2½ for brown) and adjust in ¼-cup increments, not more.

Altitude. Water boils below 212°F above sea level, so at high altitude rice needs a few extra minutes and slightly more liquid. Add about 1 tablespoon of water per cup of rice and extend the timer by 1-2 minutes per 1,000 feet.

Soaking. Soaking brown rice 30-60 minutes beforehand can shave 5-10 minutes off the 45-minute cook and improves texture. Do not soak white basmati or jasmine for more than 20-30 minutes or the grains turn fragile.

Food safety: cooked rice can make you sick

Rice is one of the higher-risk leftovers because it can carry Bacillus cereus spores that survive boiling and multiply once the rice cools. The USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service is explicit: refrigerate cooked rice within 2 hours of cooking — or within 1 hour if the room is above 90°F — because bacteria grow rapidly between 40°F and 140°F (the "danger zone") (USDA FSIS, "Leftovers and Food Safety").

Key FSIS rules applied to rice:

  • Keep cooked rice hot (140°F or above) or cold (40°F or below). Never leave a full pot on the counter to "cool all afternoon."
  • Refrigerate leftover rice for 3 to 4 days, or freeze for 3 to 4 months.
  • Reheat leftovers to 165°F as measured with a food thermometer. Note: reheating kills the bacteria but does not destroy toxins that have already formed — so timely refrigeration matters more than the reheat temperature.

For context on the safe-minimum internal temperatures of foods you'll serve alongside rice: poultry to 165°F, ground meats to 160°F, and whole cuts of beef, pork, lamb, and veal to 145°F with a 3-minute rest — all per FSIS.

Troubleshooting common rice failures

Mushy rice. Too much water or too long a cook. Drain any standing liquid, spread the rice on a tray for 5 minutes so surface moisture evaporates, and cut your next water ratio by ¼ cup.

Crunchy or undercooked center. Usually a lifted lid or too little water. Add 2 tablespoons of water, cover tightly, and cook 2-4 minutes longer — exactly the UNL recommendation above.

Scorched bottom, raw top. Heat is too high. The simmer should barely bubble. Move to a smaller burner or a diffuser and drop to the lowest setting.

Gummy, clumped grains. You skipped the rinse. Surface starch is what glues grains together; rinse white rice until the water is nearly clear and fluff with a fork (never a spoon) after resting.

Once you have the rice down, the same absorption logic carries over to other grains — see our quinoa cooking times and oatmeal cooking times.

guides.title: How Long to Cook Bacon (Stovetop, Oven & Microwave)
guides.excerpt: Cook bacon 12-20 minutes in a 400°F oven, 8-12 minutes in a skillet over medium heat, or about 1 minute per slice in the microwave. USDA FSIS says cook until crisp for safety. Times, temps, storage.
guides.author: Suraj Giri

sources.author: Fsis
sources.title: USDA FSIS — Bacon and Food Safety

sources.author: Fsis
sources.title: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart

sources.author: Thekitchn
sources.title: The Kitchn — Perfect Bacon in the Oven
The Kitchn — How To Cook Bacon in the Microwave

guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, researcher at The Blog Timer. Updated 2026-08-09.

How long to cook bacon

Cook bacon 12 to 20 minutes in a 400°F oven, 8 to 12 minutes in a skillet over medium heat, or about 1 minute per slice in the microwave. The USDA does not publish a single internal temperature for bacon because the slices are too thin to read with a thermometer; the working rule is to cook it until crisp, which the Food Safety and Inspection Service says guarantees a safe temperature (FSIS).

Bacon cooking times by method

MethodHeatRegular-cutThick-cutDoneness cue
Oven, rimmed sheet400°F~14 min (check at 12)~18 min (up to 20)Deep golden-brown, crisp
Stovetop skilletMedium (~350°F)6–10 min10–12 minBrowned, fat fully rendered
MicrowaveHigh~1 min per slice+30-sec bursts afterJust shy of desired crisp

How to cook bacon in the oven (400°F)

Heat the oven to 400°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or foil, leaving overhang on all four sides so cleanup is a fold-and-toss. Lay the strips in a single layer — close together is fine, but don't let them overlap or they'll fuse. No flipping is required. Bake until deep golden-brown and crispy: about 14 minutes for regular-cut and 18 minutes for thick-cut, beginning to check after 12 minutes (The Kitchn). Set a 12-minute timer as your first check; if you're running a full sheet of thick-cut or extra-crispy strips, plan on the full 20-minute timer, since tested recipes run 15 to 20 minutes at 400°F. For all-over crunch, set an oven-safe wire rack on the sheet so the fat drains away and the strips crisp on both sides.

How to cook bacon on the stovetop

Lay the strips in a cold dry skillet, then set the heat to medium — roughly 350°F. A cold start lets the fat render slowly so the meat cooks in its own fat instead of seizing and scorching. Turn the strips every couple of minutes as the pan comes up to temperature. FSIS cites a cooking study in which bacon fried at 350°F reached medium-well in about 6 minutes; plan on 8 to 12 minutes total for crisp, depending on thickness (FSIS). An 8-minute timer is a reliable first check for standard slices. Transfer the strips to paper towels immediately so they stop cooking in the pooled grease.

How to cook bacon in the microwave

Sandwich the strips between paper towels on a microwave-safe plate — four sheets below, two above — and microwave on high for about 1 minute per slice, then continue in 30-second bursts until the bacon is just shy of where you want it (it keeps crisping for a few seconds after it leaves the oven) (The Kitchn). The method shines for one to four slices; for a full pound, switch to the oven. Worth knowing: FSIS reports that microwaved bacon forms fewer nitrosamines than pan-fried bacon, so this is not just a convenience shortcut (FSIS).

Variables that change the cooking time

Four things move the clock. Thickness is the biggest lever — thick-cut needs 3 to 4 minutes longer than regular in any method. Starting temperature matters: strips straight from a 40°F fridge take longer than room-temperature ones. Water content varies by cure: "pumped" bacon (injected with brine) can weep a milky liquid and steam before it fries, while dry-cured bacon renders cleanly and faster. Batch size — a crowded pan drops in temperature and steams instead of crisps. FSIS also confirms it is safe to cook bacon straight from frozen (FSIS); as a general rule for cooking meat from frozen, plan on roughly 50% more time and turn the strips more often so they render evenly.

Food safety and storage

Bacon is cured pork, and FSIS notes that "if cooked crisp, it should have reached a safe temperature" — cured meat can stay pink even when fully safe, so color is not a reliable cue (FSIS). For reference, the USDA's safe-minimum chart sets pork steaks, chops and roasts at 145°F with a 3-minute rest and ground meats at 160°F (FSIS Safe Temperature Chart). Never partially cook bacon and refrigerate it to finish later — FSIS warns that surviving bacteria won't have been destroyed. Don't rinse raw bacon before cooking either; surface bacteria are killed by cooking.

For storage, FSIS lists raw bacon at 7 days refrigerated (40°F or below) or 4 months frozen, and consumer-cooked leftovers at 4 to 5 days refrigerated or 1 month frozen. Reheat precooked strips at about 10 seconds per strip in the microwave (FSIS). Serve the strips next to perfectly boiled eggs, or fold them into a smash burger.

Troubleshooting common bacon problems

  • Burnt edges, raw middle: heat too high. Drop to medium and start in a cold pan so the fat renders before the lean scorches.
  • Rubbery, never crisp: the pan was crowded or the heat too low to render. Leave space between strips and let the rendered fat do the work.
  • Curling strips: press gently with a spatula, or weigh them down; a cold-start skillet prevents most of this.
  • White foam or liquid in the pan: that's pumped (brine-injected) bacon weeping. Pour it off and lower the heat.

guides.title: How Long to Microwave Popcorn (by Wattage, Listen-for-Pops)
guides.excerpt: Microwave popcorn times by wattage, the listen-for-pops method, paper bag DIY, and stovetop comparison.
guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

Most microwave popcorn bags pop in 2-4 minutes depending on microwave wattage. The reliable method is the listen-for-pops rule: stop the microwave when pops slow to one every 2-3 seconds, not when a timer ends. A 1100W microwave pops a standard bag in 2:00-2:30; a 700W microwave needs 3:30-4:30. Cooking past the slow-pop point burns the kernels and triggers smoke alarms.

How Long Should Microwave Popcorn Take?

Most major brands — Orville Redenbacher's, Pop Secret, Jolly Time, Newman's Own — print a recommended time of 2-4 minutes on the bag, calibrated to a 1100W microwave. The actual time depends almost entirely on your microwave's wattage.

Microwave WattageStandard Bag TimeMini Bag Time
1200W+1:45 - 2:151:15 - 1:30
1100W (standard)2:00 - 2:301:30 - 1:45
1000W2:30 - 3:001:45 - 2:00
900W3:00 - 3:302:00 - 2:30
800W3:30 - 4:002:30 - 3:00
700W (compact)3:30 - 4:302:30 - 3:00

Microwave wattage is usually printed inside the door, on the back, or in the manual. Older microwaves drift lower over time as the magnetron weakens.

How Do You Use the Listen-for-Pops Method?

The bag time on the package is a starting point, not a rule. The correct stopping cue is acoustic: stop the microwave when pops slow to roughly one every 2-3 seconds, not when they have stopped entirely. By the time pops fully stop, a measurable fraction of the kernels at the bottom of the bag are already scorching.

The listen method works because popcorn pops in a tight time window — the rate accelerates from a slow start, peaks for 30-45 seconds of rapid popping, and then tapers off as the remaining un-popped kernels run out of moisture. The taper is where burning starts. Pulling the bag at the taper transition produces a fully popped bag with minimal scorch and few unpopped "old maid" kernels.

Why Do Microwaves of Different Wattages Pop So Differently?

Popcorn pops when the internal kernel temperature reaches about 356°F (180°C) and the kernel's internal moisture vaporizes explosively, rupturing the hull. Higher microwave wattage delivers more energy per second, so the popping temperature is reached faster. A 1200W microwave finishes popping in under 2 minutes; a 700W microwave needs almost twice as long because energy delivery is slower.

Within a single microwave, pop time also depends on bag position. Most modern microwaves have a turntable that distributes microwaves more evenly; without one, place the bag at the center for the most uniform cooking.

How Long for Stovetop Popcorn (for Comparison)?

Stovetop popcorn — kernels with oil in a covered pan — takes 4-6 minutes total over medium-high heat. Add 1/4 cup popcorn kernels and 2 tablespoons oil to a heavy-bottomed pan, cover, and shake occasionally. Pops begin at 2-3 minutes and finish at 5-6 minutes. The same listen-for-pops rule applies. Stovetop produces a noticeably crisper, fresher-tasting result than microwave.

Air Popper vs Microwave: Which Is Faster?

MethodTimeOilNotes
Microwave (bagged)2-4 minIn bagFastest, oiliest
Microwave (paper bag, plain kernels)3-4 minNoneDIY healthier option
Stovetop (oil)5-7 min2 TbspBest texture
Air popper3 minNoneNo oil, fluffy result
Whirley Pop (hand crank)4-5 minOptionalTheater-style

Can You Microwave Plain Kernels in a Paper Bag?

Yes. Add 1/4 cup popcorn kernels to a brown paper lunch bag, fold the top down twice, and microwave 2-4 minutes (listen-for-pops). This produces oil-free popcorn at a fraction of the cost of bagged microwave popcorn. Season after popping with salt, melted butter, or nutritional yeast.

Why Does Microwave Popcorn Sometimes Burn?

Burning happens when the bag stays in past the pop-rate taper. The bottom of the bag — sitting against the warmest surface — receives continued microwave energy after most kernels have popped, charring them. Modern microwaves include a popcorn button that uses humidity sensors to detect when popping slows; results vary. The listen method is more reliable.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long do you microwave a bag of popcorn?

2-4 minutes for a standard bag, depending on your microwave wattage. Stop when pops slow to one every 2-3 seconds.

What does the popcorn button do?

It uses a humidity sensor to detect when steam from popping kernels drops, then stops the microwave. Results vary by microwave model.

Can I microwave popcorn for 5 minutes?

Almost certainly too long. Most standard bags burn before 5 minutes even in compact microwaves.

Why is my microwave popcorn so chewy?

Under-popped (still has moisture inside the puffed kernel) or sitting too long in the bag steaming. Open the bag immediately after popping.

How long to microwave half a bag?

Half the popcorn does not mean half the time — kernels need consistent energy. Use the full bag or a smaller "mini" bag designed for that volume.

What is the perfect popcorn time?

For a 1100W microwave with a standard bag, 2:15-2:30 is typical. Calibrate by listening on your first bag, then memorize the number.

Can microwave popcorn explode?

The bag can ignite if cooked far too long; this is the most common cause of microwave fires. Never leave popcorn unattended.

For full citations and methodology, see our sources page.

guides.title: How Long to Air Fry Chicken (Breasts, Thighs & Tenders)
guides.excerpt: Air fry chicken at 375-400°F: boneless breasts 15-20 min, boneless thighs 18-22 min, bone-in thighs 25-30 min, tenders 10-12 min, always to 165°F internal. USDA-cited chart and method.
guides.author: Suraj Giri

sources.author: Fsis
sources.title: USDA FSIS - Air Fryers and Food Safety

sources.author: Uaex
sources.title: University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture Extension - Ten Cooking Tips for Your Air Fryer

sources.author: Springermountainfarms
sources.title: Springer Mountain Farms - How to Cook Chicken in an Air Fryer

guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, researcher at The Blog Timer. Updated 2026-08-09.

The Short Answer: 10 to 30 Minutes at 375-400°F

Air fry boneless, skinless chicken breasts for 15-20 minutes at 375°F, boneless thighs for 18-22 minutes at 380°F, bone-in thighs for 25-30 minutes at 380°F, and chicken tenders for 10-12 minutes at 375°F — flipping halfway. The USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) confirms air fryers generally cook foods in 5 to 25 minutes at 350-400°F, and that all poultry is only safe once it reaches an internal temperature of 165°F. Use a food thermometer; time alone is never the safety test.

Air Fryer Chicken Time and Temperature Chart

These times assume a preheated basket, a single uncrowded layer, and a flip at the halfway mark. They are corroborated by manufacturer guidance from Springer Mountain Farms' air-fryer cooking chart and align with the temperature band FSIS publishes for air fryers.

CutTemperatureTimeSafe Internal Temp
Chicken tenders / tenderloins375°F10-12 min165°F
Boneless, skinless breasts (8 oz)375°F15-20 min165°F
Bone-in, skin-on breasts375°F30-35 min165°F
Boneless thighs380°F18-22 min165°F
Bone-in thighs380°F25-30 min165°F
Drumsticks380°F25-30 min165°F
Wings400°F20-25 min165°F
Ground chicken patties375°F12-15 min165°F (ground poultry; 160°F applies only to ground beef/pork)

For boneless thighs, set a 18-minute timer to check at the low end and a 22-minute timer as the upper bound. For bone-in thighs or drumsticks, start with a 25-minute timer and verify the thermometer reads 165°F.

How to Air Fry Chicken Breasts

Pat the breasts dry, lightly oil them, season, and lay them in a single layer — FSIS warns that overcrowding blocks air circulation and causes uneven or undercooked food, so cook in batches if needed. Set 375°F and run 15-20 minutes for an 8 oz boneless breast, flipping at the 8-minute mark. The University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture Extension breads boneless breasts and air fries them at 375°F for 7 minutes, then flips and air fries 7-10 minutes more (14-17 minutes total), until a thermometer reads 165°F. For thicker (10-12 oz) breasts, push toward the 20-minute end. Set a 20-minute timer for an 8 oz breast and start checking at 15. If you prefer the oven method instead, see how long to bake chicken.

How to Air Fry Thighs (Boneless and Bone-In)

Thighs carry more fat than breasts, so they stay juicy and tolerate the higher 380°F setting well. Boneless thighs need 18-22 minutes; bone-in thighs need 25-30 minutes because the bone slows heat transfer. Skin-on thighs crisp better if you start skin-side down and flip skin-side up for the second half so the rendered fat bastes the surface. Insert the thermometer in the thickest part of the meat, making sure not to touch bone, fat, or gristle, which would give a falsely high reading.

How to Air Fry Chicken Tenders

Tenders are the fastest cut — 10-12 minutes at 375°F, flipped once. Because they are thin, they overcook fast, so set a 12-minute timer and check at 10. Breaded tenders (cornflake, panko, or a flour-egg-breadcrumb station) benefit from a 1-second oil spray so the coating browns instead of drying out. FSIS specifically cautions that raw, stuffed breaded chicken breast products should not be cooked in an air fryer — follow the manufacturer instructions on those packaged items instead, since the air fryer may not heat the stuffed center to a safe temperature.

Variables That Change the Time

  • Thickness. A 6 oz thin-cut breast finishes near 12 minutes; a 12 oz breast can need 22-25. Pound uneven breasts to even thickness so the thin end does not dry out.
  • Bone-in vs. boneless. Bone slows heat transfer and adds roughly 5-10 minutes.
  • Frozen vs. fresh. Cooking from frozen adds about 50% to the time; FSIS stresses the thermometer is the only reliable doneness test regardless of starting temperature.
  • Preheating. A 3-minute preheat at the target temperature shortens cook time and improves browning. Without it, add 2-3 minutes.
  • Batch size. A loaded basket drops air temperature and lengthens the cook; the University of Arkansas Extension notes overfilling interferes with browning and even cooking.

For a smokier alternative to the air fryer, see how long to grill chicken.

Food Safety: The 165°F Rule

Chicken is safe to eat only when it reaches 165°F internal, measured in the thickest part. FSIS lists these safe minimum internal temperatures: poultry and ground poultry 165°F; ground meats 160°F; whole cuts of beef, pork, veal, and lamb 145°F with a 3-minute rest; fish 145°F. Refrigerate any leftover chicken within 2 hours — FSIS defines the Danger Zone as 40-140°F, where bacteria multiply rapidly. To reheat, the Arkansas Extension recommends setting the air fryer to 300°F and reheating until the food again reads 165°F.

Troubleshooting Common Problems

Burnt outside, raw inside: Temperature is too high or pieces are too thick. Drop to 360°F, add 4-5 minutes, and finish with a probe. Pale, rubbery skin: The basket was crowded or the skin was wet — pat dry, leave space, and raise the last 2 minutes to 400°F. Dry breast: You overcooked it — pull the moment the thermometer hits 165°F and rest 5 minutes so juices redistribute (FSIS's official safe minimum is 165°F; resting does not replace reaching it). Uneven cooking: You skipped the flip — the top of an air fryer runs hotter than the bottom, so turn everything at the halfway mark.

guides.title: How Long to Cook Pasta (Al Dente Times by Shape)
guides.excerpt: Pasta cooking times by shape with al dente science, water-to-salt ratios, and Instant Pot conversions.
guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

Most dried pasta cooks in 8-12 minutes in well-salted boiling water. The box time is a guideline — start tasting one minute before the box says, and pull when the pasta has slight resistance at the center (al dente). Long shapes (spaghetti, linguine, fettuccine) average 8-11 minutes; short shapes (penne, rotini, fusilli) 10-12 minutes; stuffed pasta (ravioli, tortellini) 3-5 minutes. Fresh pasta needs only 2-4 minutes.

What Does Al Dente Actually Mean?

Al dente — Italian for "to the tooth" — describes pasta that is fully cooked but still firm enough to push back against the bite, with a thin, light-colored core just visible when a noodle is sliced. Al dente pasta has a lower glycemic index than fully soft pasta and holds sauce better because the surface starches are less developed. The Italian Academy of Cuisine recommends al dente as the only acceptable doneness for the country's pasta tradition.

The science: pasta cooks in two stages. First, water penetrates the dried gluten-starch matrix and gelatinizes the starch granules. Second, continued cooking softens the gluten network. Pulling pasta at al dente captures the first stage complete and the second stage just begun.

Cooking Time by Shape

ShapeBox TimeAl Dente Target
Angel hair (capellini)3-5 min3-4 min
Spaghetti8-12 min8-10 min
Linguine9-12 min9-11 min
Fettuccine10-12 min10-11 min
Penne10-13 min10-11 min
Rigatoni12-15 min11-12 min
Rotini / Fusilli10-12 min9-10 min
Farfalle (bowtie)10-12 min10-11 min
Orzo8-10 min8-9 min
Macaroni (elbows)7-9 min7-8 min
Lasagna sheets10-12 min8-10 min (par-cook)
Orecchiette11-13 min10-12 min
Fresh pasta (any shape)2-4 min2-3 min
Ravioli (filled)4-6 min4-5 min
Tortellini (filled)3-5 min3-4 min
Gnocchi (potato)2-3 minFloat + 30 sec

How Much Water and Salt?

The Italian standard is 1 liter of water and 10 grams of salt per 100 grams of pasta (roughly 4 quarts water and 2 tablespoons salt per pound). Generous water gives noodles room to move and dilutes the released starch; generous salt seasons the pasta from inside (sauce alone cannot reach the noodle interior). The salt also slightly raises water temperature — a small effect.

The popular myth that adding oil prevents sticking is false in practice — oil floats on top and contributes little to noodle separation. Stirring in the first minute after adding pasta is what prevents sticking.

How Do You Know When Pasta Is Done?

The reliable method is to taste a noodle starting 1 minute before the box time. The noodle should bite with slight resistance and the center should show a thin, light-colored line. The bite should feel pleasant, not chalky. Once you reach this point, immediately drain — pasta continues cooking from residual heat.

The visual cue: a snapped noodle should show a thin white center about the thickness of a single hair. A completely uniform color means the pasta is past al dente.

Should You Save Pasta Water?

Yes — always reserve at least 1 cup of starchy pasta water before draining. The dissolved starch acts as a sauce thickener and emulsifier, particularly important for oil-based sauces (cacio e pepe, aglio e olio) and tomato sauces that need to cling to noodles. Stir 2-4 tablespoons of pasta water into the sauce-noodle combination just before serving.

Does Pasta Need to Rest Like Other Foods?

No. Pasta should go directly from drain to sauce. Pasta sitting in a colander for more than 30 seconds clumps and gets sticky as residual heat continues to cook surface starches. The faster you sauce, the better the result.

How Long to Cook Pasta in the Instant Pot?

Pressure-cooker pasta times: take the box time, divide by 2, and subtract 1 minute. Spaghetti rated 10 minutes on the box cooks at 4 minutes high pressure. Add 8 cups water per pound of pasta in the Instant Pot, plus sauce.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long to cook spaghetti?

8-10 minutes for al dente. Box time is usually 10-12 minutes; pull a minute earlier.

Why does my pasta stick together?

Not enough water, or not stirring in the first minute. The starch released by raw pasta is gummy until diluted.

How much pasta per person?

2 oz (56 g) dry pasta per person as a side; 4 oz (113 g) as a main.

Should you rinse pasta?

No — except for cold pasta salad. Rinsing washes off the starch that helps sauce cling.

How long to cook fresh pasta?

2-4 minutes total. Fresh pasta is much more delicate; check after 2 minutes.

Does pasta cook faster in a covered pot?

Not significantly — the water is already at boiling temperature.

How to fix overcooked pasta?

You cannot reverse it, but cold-rinsing and shocking in ice water stops further cooking. Use it for a cold salad rather than serving hot.

What pasta cooks fastest?

Angel hair (capellini), fresh egg pasta, and small shapes like orzo. All are under 5 minutes.

For full citations and methodology, see our sources page.

guides.title: How Long to Defrost Chicken (Fridge, Cold Water, Microwave)
guides.excerpt: Safe defrost times for chicken — USDA refrigerator, cold-water, microwave methods, plus what is unsafe.
guides.author: Suraj Giri

sources.author: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperatures

guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

Defrost chicken safely using one of three USDA-approved methods: refrigerator (24 hours per 5 pounds, slowest but safest), cold water (30 minutes per pound, faster), or microwave (3-10 minutes total, fastest but must cook immediately). The USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service explicitly warns against thawing chicken on the counter — bacterial growth in the temperature "danger zone" (40-140°F) makes it unsafe.

How Long to Defrost Chicken in the Refrigerator?

Refrigerator thawing is the safest method because chicken stays below 40°F (4°C) — outside the bacterial danger zone — the entire time. The USDA guideline is 24 hours per 5 pounds of chicken, with whole chickens needing the full 24 hours and individual pieces taking less.

Chicken TypeRefrigerator Thaw Time
Boneless breasts (1-2 lb)12-24 hours
Bone-in pieces (2-3 lb)24 hours
Whole chicken (3-4 lb)24-30 hours
Whole chicken (5 lb)30-36 hours
Ground chicken (1 lb)12-24 hours
Frozen wings (3 lb)24 hours

Place the chicken on a plate or in a container to catch any drips, and store on the lowest shelf of the fridge to prevent cross-contamination. Thawed chicken can be safely held in the refrigerator for 1-2 days after thawing before cooking, per USDA.

How Long to Defrost Chicken in Cold Water?

The cold-water method is significantly faster while remaining safe — about 30 minutes per pound. Place the chicken in a leak-proof zip-top bag (this is essential to prevent water absorption and bacterial entry), submerge in a bowl or pot of cold water, and change the water every 30 minutes to keep the temperature low enough to inhibit bacterial growth.

Chicken WeightCold Water Time
1 lb (boneless breasts)30-45 min
2 lb1 - 1.5 hr
3 lb1.5 - 2 hr
4-5 lb whole chicken2 - 3 hr

Chicken thawed by the cold-water method must be cooked immediately, not refrigerated for later — the temperature climbs into the danger zone briefly during thawing and bacterial populations can grow if held.

How Long to Defrost Chicken in the Microwave?

Microwave thawing is the fastest method (3-10 minutes for a single breast) but requires immediate cooking afterward. Use the microwave's defrost setting if available, or 30% power manually. Approximately 6-8 minutes per pound at 30% power. The chicken will be partially cooked in spots — this is unavoidable. The USDA permits microwave thawing but requires that the meat be cooked immediately because warm spots have entered the danger zone.

What Defrosting Methods Are Unsafe?

Per the USDA, the following are not safe for defrosting chicken:

  • Counter (room temperature). The surface enters the danger zone within an hour. Bacteria multiply rapidly.
  • Hot water. Surface enters the danger zone immediately.
  • Out in sun or near a heat source. Same problem.
  • In a slow cooker (raw, frozen). The slow cooker takes too long to bring chicken out of the danger zone — even on high.

Cooking frozen chicken without thawing is safe — just takes 50% longer than thawed chicken.

Method Comparison

MethodTime (1 lb)Time (4 lb whole)SafetyQuality
Refrigerator12-24 hr24-30 hrBestBest
Cold water30-45 min2-3 hrGood (with changes)Good
Microwave4-8 min15-25 minAcceptableReduced
Cook from frozenN/AN/ASafeReduced
CounterN/AN/AUNSAFEN/A

Can You Refreeze Chicken After Thawing?

Per USDA: yes, if the chicken was thawed in the refrigerator and still feels cold. Do not refreeze chicken thawed in cold water or microwave unless it has been cooked first. Refrozen raw chicken loses some moisture and texture but is safe.

How to Tell if Chicken Is Fully Defrosted

  1. No ice crystals visible when poking with a fork.
  2. Flesh is pliable — bends without resistance.
  3. No frozen core when pressed at the thickest part.
  4. Internal temperature 34-38°F if you have a thermometer — refrigerator-cold.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I defrost chicken in hot water?

No. Hot water raises surface temperature into the danger zone immediately, allowing bacterial growth.

How long can defrosted chicken stay in the fridge?

1-2 days after thawing, per USDA. Cook within that window.

Is it safe to cook frozen chicken without thawing?

Yes — increase cook time by about 50%. Use a thermometer to confirm 165°F internal.

Why is counter thawing unsafe?

The surface warms past 40°F (the danger-zone threshold) before the core thaws, allowing bacterial growth on the exterior.

Can I thaw chicken in the slow cooker?

No. The slow cooker holds food too long in the danger zone before cooking.

How long does it take to defrost a whole chicken?

24-30 hours in the refrigerator for a 4-pound whole chicken; 2-3 hours in cold water with water changes every 30 minutes.

Can I refreeze chicken after thawing?

Only if thawed in the refrigerator. Microwave and cold-water thawed chicken must be cooked first.

guides.title: How Long to Boil Potatoes (Whole, Cubed, for Mashing or Salad)
guides.excerpt: Boiling times for potatoes — whole vs cubed, by size, for mashing vs salad, starting cold-water method.
guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

Boil whole small potatoes in 15-20 minutes, whole medium potatoes in 20-25 minutes, large in 30-40 minutes, and cubed potatoes (1-inch) in 10-15 minutes. Start potatoes in cold salted water, bring to a boil, then simmer at medium heat until a fork or knife slides through with no resistance. For mashing, use starchy russets; for salad, use waxy Yukon Golds or red potatoes.

How Long to Boil Whole Potatoes?

Time depends on size, not weight. The center of the potato must reach about 205-210°F (96-99°C) for the starch to fully gelatinize, and heat must travel from the boiling water's surface temperature (212°F at sea level) to that center.

Potato SizeDiameterWhole Boil Time
Baby / new potatoes1-1.5 in10-15 min
Small2 in15-20 min
Medium2.5-3 in20-25 min
Large3.5-4 in30-40 min
Extra large4+ in40-50 min

How Long for Cubed Potatoes?

Cubed potatoes cook dramatically faster because heat penetrates from all sides simultaneously. Standard 1-inch cubes take 10-15 minutes; 1/2-inch cubes take 7-10 minutes; 2-inch chunks take 15-20 minutes. For mashed potatoes, larger cubes (1.5-2 inches) absorb less water and produce a less watery mash.

Why Start Potatoes in Cold Water?

This is the most consistently broken rule in home cooking. Starting potatoes in cold water means the interior and exterior cook at the same rate as the water gradually heats. Throwing potatoes into already-boiling water cooks the exterior much faster than the interior — by the time the center is done, the outer layer is mushy and waterlogged.

Cold-water start is especially important for whole potatoes. For 1/2-inch dice, the time difference is small enough that hot-water start is acceptable.

How Much Salt in the Water?

Generously — about 1 tablespoon of kosher salt per quart of water, or "salty like the sea." Salt seasons the potato through the boil rather than just the surface, and it slightly raises water temperature (a small effect). Unsalted boiled potatoes taste flat no matter how much salt you add at the table.

For Mashing vs. For Salad: Which Potato?

UseBest PotatoWhy
MashedRusset (Idaho)High starch, low moisture — fluffy result
Mashed (creamy)Yukon GoldMedium starch, buttery flavor
Potato saladRed potatoesWaxy, holds shape
Potato saladYukon GoldSlight starch, creamy texture
Boiled for sidesYukon Gold, red, fingerlingsHolds shape on the plate
Soup / chowderYukon GoldStays intact, thickens lightly
RoastedRusset or Yukon GoldCrisps well

How to Tell When Boiled Potatoes Are Done

  1. Knife test. A paring knife slides into the thickest part with no resistance — but does not so easily that the potato falls apart.
  2. Fork test. A fork tine penetrates and exits cleanly.
  3. Visual. Skin starts to crack slightly. (Stop here for potato salad; overcooked potatoes lose their shape.)

Drain immediately when done. Potatoes left in hot water continue absorbing moisture and become waterlogged.

What About Boiling for Mashed Potatoes?

For the best mashed potato texture, boil peeled russet potatoes cubed into 1.5-2 inch chunks, starting in cold salted water, for about 15-20 minutes until fork-tender. Drain, then return to the hot pan over low heat for 30 seconds to evaporate any clinging surface moisture. Mash while still hot. Cold potatoes glue up the starch and produce gummy mash.

What About Boiling for Potato Salad?

For potato salad, boil whole small red or Yukon Gold potatoes (skin on) in salted water, starting cold, for 18-22 minutes. Drain, let cool to room temperature, then cube. The cooler temperature firms the starch so cubes hold their shape in the salad. Hot potatoes added directly to dressing produce a mushy salad.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long to boil potatoes for mashed potatoes?

15-20 minutes for 1.5-2 inch cubes of russet potatoes, starting in cold salted water.

How long to boil whole potatoes?

Small whole potatoes: 15-20 min. Medium: 20-25 min. Large: 30-40 min.

Do you boil potatoes in cold or hot water?

Cold water. Lets the inside and outside cook at the same rate.

How long to boil red potatoes?

About 15-20 minutes for small whole red potatoes (1.5-2 inch diameter).

Should I peel potatoes before boiling?

For mashed: yes. For potato salad and side dishes: optional — skins add texture and nutrition.

Why are my boiled potatoes gummy?

Over-mashed, or mashed cold. Mash while still hot and stop before they look glossy.

How long to boil baby potatoes?

About 10-15 minutes for 1-1.5 inch baby or "new" potatoes.

Can I boil potatoes ahead of time?

Yes. Boil, drain, cool, and refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in the microwave or by re-warming in the oven.

guides.title: Best Pomodoro Apps in 2026 (Focus Keeper, Forest, Pomofocus)
guides.excerpt: The 8 best Pomodoro apps compared — Focus Keeper, Forest, Be Focused, Pomofocus, Marinara, Toggl, TickTick, Notion.
guides.content:
By Suraj Giri, Productivity Researcher · Updated 2026-05-27

The best Pomodoro apps in 2026 are Focus Keeper (iOS, paid features), Forest (gamified, iOS/Android), Be Focused (iOS/Mac), Pomofocus.io (browser-free), Marinara Timer (browser-free), Toggl Track (Pomodoro mode), TickTick (built-in), and Notion (DIY). The right choice depends on whether you value gamification, multi-device sync, time tracking, or task management integration. For pure browser use without signup, our Pomodoro timer covers the essentials.

What Makes a Good Pomodoro App?

A Pomodoro app should at minimum deliver three things: a reliable 25-minute timer with audio alert, an automatic break timer, and a visible session counter to track sets of four pomodoros. Beyond these basics, apps differentiate on task management, statistics, multi-device sync, gamification, and integrations with calendars and to-do apps. The classic Pomodoro Technique requires very little software — Francesco Cirillo's original used a wind-up tomato.

1. Focus Keeper

One of the most polished iOS apps. Clean interface, customizable intervals, statistics dashboard, and Apple Watch support. Free version offers full Pomodoro functionality; the Pro tier ($1.99) unlocks unlimited sessions and analytics. Best for users invested in the Apple ecosystem who want a minimal, dedicated tool.

2. Forest

The most popular gamified Pomodoro app. When you start a focus session, a virtual tree begins to grow; abandoning the session kills the tree. Over time you build a forest of completed sessions. The premium tier ($3.99) plants real trees through the partner organization Trees for the Future. Cross-platform (iOS, Android, web). The visualization tricks the dopamine system into staying with focus.

3. Be Focused

Native Apple ecosystem app for iOS, iPad, and Mac. Tasks, sessions, and statistics all sync via iCloud. The Pro version ($1.99) removes ads and unlocks themes. Best for users who want Pomodoro + lightweight task management without leaving Apple's design language.

4. Pomofocus.io

Browser-based, free, no signup required. Clean interface, task list, customizable intervals. Sounds and themes built in. The most popular free web Pomodoro and what many users adopt before realizing they want more features. Trade-off: no native mobile app and no cloud sync without account.

5. Marinara Timer

The minimalist's pick. A single web page with three modes (Pomodoro, custom, kitchen). Shareable URL means a team can run synchronized pomodoros. No signup, no tracking, no ads. Open-source project that has been around since 2012. Best for shared remote work sprints.

6. Toggl Track

A full time-tracking platform with a Pomodoro mode built in. The advantage: every pomodoro becomes a tracked time entry tagged to a project or client. Free tier covers Pomodoro use; paid tiers add reporting and team features. Best for freelancers and consultants who need to bill for time.

7. TickTick

A to-do app with a built-in Pomodoro timer that links sessions to specific tasks. When you complete a session, it logs against the task and contributes to weekly statistics. Free tier includes the Pomodoro feature; the $3/month Premium adds detailed habit tracking. Best for users who want one app for tasks + focus.

8. Notion

Not a dedicated Pomodoro app, but the platform's flexibility lets users build custom Pomodoro databases that link sessions to tasks, projects, and habits. A growing number of templates exist on the Notion gallery. Best for users already deep in Notion's ecosystem.
